### Superconductors
Superconductors are materials that exhibit zero electrical resistance and complete diamagnetism (Meissner effect) when cooled below a characteristic critical temperature ($T_c$).

### Difference Between Type-I and Type-II Superconductors

| Property | Type-I Superconductors | Type-II Superconductors |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Magnetic Behavior** | Complete Meissner effect; abruptly loses superconductivity at a low critical field ($H_c$). | Two critical fields ($H_{c1}$ and $H_{c2}$); exhibits a mixed state of partial magnetic flux penetration. |
| **Material Type** | Mostly pure soft metals (e.g., Lead, Mercury). | Mostly alloys and transition metal compounds (e.g., $Nb_3Sn$, $YBa_2Cu_3O_7$). |
| **Applications** | Limited practical use due to low critical magnetic fields. | Extensively used in high-field electromagnets and MRI machines. |
proTip: Type-II superconductors are technologically more important because they can sustain much higher magnetic fields before losing superconductivity.
